body:
When a dynamic orchestrator root resumes without its turn boundary checkpoint (a lost transcript store, or a crash before the first boundary), it regenerates the spawn turn instead of continuing past it. The recovery path for that shape compared only agentType and prompt at a colliding ordinal, but recovery advances the ordinal counter past every journaled admission, so the collision could not occur: instrumentation across the full suite showed zero hits on that branch. Every regenerated spawn therefore re-decided and re-paid its child even with an identical spec, and the eighteenth comparison benchmark separately flagged the two field comparison as a stale child hazard had it fired (a changed model hint, schema, or toolset reference would have adopted a child produced under the old spec).

Adoption is now content addressed. recover() indexes unclaimed journaled admissions by jcsSerialize over the full spec; a regenerated call whose spec matches byte for byte claims the first such decision in journal order, with the settled child replaying free, a dangling one redispatching pinned to its journaled scope, and a recovered rejection rolling forward typed. A call diverging in any field decides fresh, and the prior decision's child stays paid (at least once semantics). Checkpoint continued resumes are untouched: they never re-execute the spawn turn.

Verification: two crash and resume tests pin the free replay on an identical spec and the fresh decision on divergence (116 tests in orchestrate.test.ts, 3273 vitest green); the manifest grows to 291 probes, all killed (disabling the spec claim re-decides the child and the named killer catches the double payment); full gates green including the docs site.

author: elares
body:
feat(admin): mount the risk posture reads, so "flagged for review" can actually be reviewed

The disavowal page tells a user, in these words, that choosing "This wasn't me" will "flag your
credentials for review". Consuming a disavowal is what sets that flag. Nothing could read it.

Measured: `credentials_flagged_for_review`, `latest_decision` and `get_decision` all had ZERO
production callers, and the published management contract carried no risk operation at all. So the
promise was unreviewable in the strict sense. A user reported that a login was not theirs, the
system recorded it, and no operator had any way to find the accounts that had been reported.

This is the third dead-surface of the same family this session (#525 magic link, #526 SMS OTP,
#527 and #528 the confirmation GETs), and it was found the same way: enumerate store methods with
no production caller, then ask what the doc comment says the method was FOR. This one says "for the
account view, audit sampling, or reconstruction".

No migration, and that is the measured difference from #526
-------------------------------------------------------------

The SMS surface needed migration 0105 because 0050 granted its tables to `ironauth_app` alone.
Here migration 0054 ALREADY granted `SELECT ON risk_decisions` and `SELECT ON risk_disavowal_tokens`
to `ironauth_control`, deliberately, and 0072 refers back to that grant as precedent. So the control
plane could always have read these rows. Only the surface was missing, and the fix is a surface with
no privilege change at all.

Two routes, both reads, on the existing diagnostics family
------------------------------------------------------------

`GET .../diagnostics/risk/users/{user_id}` reports whether the account is flagged and its latest
decision. `GET .../diagnostics/risk/decisions/{decision_id}` reads one decision by id, which is what
makes an audit row naming a decision reconstructable, the use its own doc names.

The signals document is returned PARSED rather than as an opaque string, so a diagnostic is
readable without a second decode step. A document that fails to parse becomes JSON `null` rather
than failing the whole read: the column is written by this system, so a malformed one is a defect an
operator should SEE in a diagnostic, not a reason to deny them the score and action too.

Both go through `require_environment` and the id parses in scope, so a decision minted in another
environment is the uniform not-found rather than a cross-environment read of another tenant's login
telemetry. Asserted directly.

The test that stops the headline being vacuous
------------------------------------------------

The flag's TRUE branch is the whole point, so it is driven end to end, and the ordering is what
makes it mean something. ISSUING a disavowal token is asserted NOT to flag the account: the user has
been offered the link and has not acted on it. Only CONSUMING it flags. Without that first
assertion, a posture that reported every account holding a token would look identical on the happy
path and the test would pass for the wrong reason.

The other four tests cover the unscored baseline (a legible 200 with a null decision, since an
operator asking "has this been flagged" needs an answer and "no" is one), latest-versus-by-id
addressing across two recorded decisions, the uniform not-found for an absent user and for both a
malformed and an absent decision id, and cross-environment invisibility.

Decisions are recorded through the DATA plane in these tests, because `ironauth_app` is the role
0054 grants INSERT to. The management surface only ever reads, which is the plane split working as
intended rather than an inconvenience.

Verification
--------------

Local gate green end to end. Five new tests. All five contract sweeps updated: `openapi_contract`
(two operation ids, two method and path entries, the route count 173 to 175), `live_surface`, and
`absent_environment`, `unsealed_environment` and `deleted_environment` verified as needing nothing
(both routes are reads, and the two write sweeps drive writes). `MINIMUM_ENTRIES` is raised 227 to
228. OpenAPI, SPA bindings and embed regenerated; the route audit is clean.

With this the risk reads are wired and the store audit that produced this run of PRs has nothing
actionable left in `repository.rs`: of the four methods that remain callerless, `count_dynamic` is
measured redundant (the DCR quota is enforced inside the registration transaction),
`local_cutover_mark` is documented WRITE-AND-REPORT ONLY by its own doc comment, and the two
interchange accessors plus `visibility_of` and `challenge_status` are unused helpers rather than
dormant controls.

body:
**Stacked on #35**, which is stacked on #34. Base is `feat/access-tokens`, so the diff here is only the ingest work. Merge #34 → #35 → this.

Split out of #35, which had grown to cover both auth and the whole template storage path.

From [`01-template-storage-and-chunk-model`](.scratch/v1/issues/01-template-storage-and-chunk-model.md). Green at `f4773f4`: `lint`, `check`, `test` (**454**, from 377), `build`.

## The pipeline

`POST /admin/templates` → decode → quantise → slice → encode each chunk → hash → put → three D1 rows. `GET /chunks/:hash` serves them back.

**A minimal PNG codec** (`packages/shared/src/png.ts`). Ingest runs in a Worker: no canvas, and `sharp` is a Node addon. Accepts 8-bit non-interlaced greyscale/RGB/indexed/grey+alpha/RGBA, emits 8-bit indexed, rejects everything else loudly. Deflate comes from `CompressionStream`, so there is no bundled zlib and no dependency. The narrowness is deliberate — uploads are admin-only and rare, so a narrow input surface costs an operator one clear message and removes a class of parser bug from a path that writes to permanent storage.

**Quantising** maps each pixel to its nearest palette colour, memoised by distinct colour — the affordability argument, since a real image has few. Alpha is a threshold at 128 rather than part of the metric, because folding it in would match opaque entries against translucent pixels. The upload response reports share moved, mean and max distance, and distinct colours used: that reporting is what replaced the old reject-anything-non-conformant rule.

**Slicing** cuts on wplace's tile boundaries. The bbox is the painted extent, not the image rect — a transparent margin would otherwise enlarge the box that culling, overlap detection and the progress ceiling all read. A tile the template merely spans but paints nothing in produces no chunk.

**Storage is content-addressed**, so identical content is stored once: hashes are deduplicated into a map and checked with a single `hasAll`, which is why that port method exists. Two tiles carrying the same cropped image share one blob, and re-uploading an unchanged template writes nothing.

## The palette was wrong, and is fixed here

Ticket 09 recorded 59 colours recovered by clustering one real `.wplace` file, stating "the underlying modes are exact palette values". They were not — clustering recovers modes, and the mode of a noisy distribution is not the value that generated it:

- Five entries sat 1–2 off the real colour (`#F8A90A` for `#F6AA09`, and four more).
- `#180006` sat 24 from black and is not a wplace colour at all.
- Ten real colours were missing.

Under the original rule, five real colours would have been rejected and one non-colour accepted. Replaced with wplace's own ordered palette from `mia-cx/ditherette`: 31 free at 0–30, 32 premium at 31–62, **transparent at 63**. That resolves both of ticket 09's open items and brings the free/premium split `14-v1-viewing-modes` needs.

**The index is the contract** — paint requests carry indices, not RGB — so chunks store wplace's index directly and the full 64-entry palette is written into every chunk PNG. A subset palette would make the same byte mean different colours in different chunks.

## Notes

- `uuidV7()` is monotonic within a millisecond. `crypto.randomUUID()` is v4 and the wire rejects it; verified against the canonical pattern over 5,000 ids, all unique and sorting in generation order.
- The three D1 rows go in one `batch()`, ordered so `current_version_id` is set after the version it references exists — the relationship is circular and D1 has no deferred foreign keys.
- Ticket 01 lists `{tile, offset, hash, w, h}` as the chunk record; the wire keeps `{tile, hash}` and that is right. A chunk is exactly `bbox ∩ tile`, so offset and size are derivable — storing them would create a disagreement that currently cannot exist.

## Not in this slice

Wrapped placement: a template running past the east edge is rejected rather than wrapped. The wire supports `minX > maxX`, so it is a coherent feature, but it needs a decision nothing has made — which of the two runs is the bbox's `minX`. Failing loudly beat silently placing pixels across the canvas.

Manifest assembly and `GET /manifest` are next, and are what make any of this visible to a client.
